Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at Example 1 (2024-09-24):

History shows prices drifting lower from ~71 to ~63.5 over 18 days.
The model forecasts are also lower but seem to be undershooting the true outcomes in some places and overcorrecting in others.

Let me look at the differences between model and true outcomes:

Model forecast vs True outcome for Example 1:

At the beginning (days 1-5):
- Model: [63.79, 65.04, 66.14, 65.78, 65.22]
- True: [63.87, 65.24, 66.52, 66.33, 65.56]
Differences: [-0.08, -0.20, -0.38, -0.55, -0.34]

The model is consistently undershooting (more bearish) than reality by 0.3-0.6 points on average for the first 5 days.

Looking at sentiment:
- Initial sentiment is high (1.00, 1.00, 1.00) matching the price dip
- Then sentiment becomes more mixed

Let me look at Example 3 (2024-02-02) which shows a clearer pattern:

History: prices drifting from 72.06 down to 62.32 over 18 days
Model forecast: starts at 63.86, trending down to 54.58
True outcome: starts at 63.50, trending down to 55.42
